types.name: FDebrisPool
types.doc:
The per-scene debris budget. Every shard a break spawns is entered here;
when the count would pass the budget the OLDEST shard is recycled first,
and no shard outlives the lifetime cap whatever its component asked for.
Without this a cascade in a room full of crates spawned bodies until the
physics step could not keep its budget, and "keep forever" pieces (a
lifetime of 0) never left at all.

members.name: MaxCount
members.doc: phys.Debris.MaxCount / phys.Debris.MaxLifetime.

members.name: MaxSpawnPerFrame
members.doc:
phys.Debris.MaxSpawnPerFrame: shards one update may create across every
break. A break past it spawns fewer pieces rather than a hitch; the
count restarts at each Tick.

members.name: SetBudgetOverride
members.doc:
A test (or a scene that knows better) can pin the budget without
touching the cvars; negative restores the cvar.

members.name: ClampLifetime
members.doc: 0 means "keep" on the component; under a budget that becomes the cap.

members.name: Forget

The entity went away some other way (its own cascade break, a scene

members.name: cascadeLevels
members.doc:
Multi-level fracture: debris pieces inherit a Destructible with
one level less, half the piece count, and a raised impact threshold —
hard hits shatter the shards again. 0 = single-level (default).

members.name: fractureAssetPath
members.doc:
An offline carve (.fracture, the details block's Bake Fracture button).
Empty means the Voronoi clipper runs on the game thread at break time,
which is what a prop with sixty pieces cannot afford mid-firefight, and
what leaves two peers carving from whatever collider each of them has.

members.name: replicateBreaks
members.doc:
The server owns breaks. With this on, a break on the host sends one
(chunk set, seed, impulse) event and every client replays the same
shards from its own bake; off, the entity simply vanishes on clients
when its ghost despawns.

members.name: partialDamage
members.doc:
Partial damage: a hit releases only the pieces within Damage Radius
of it, the rest stays standing as a remnant, and any part of the
remnant that no longer reaches an anchored piece through shared faces
falls with it. Off, a hit breaks the whole prop as before.

members.name: anchor
members.doc:
Which side of the prop holds it up: pieces touching that side of the
fractured bounds are anchored. None anchors nothing, so any partial
hit drops everything the hit did not already release.

members.name: MulticastPointDamage
members.signature: void MulticastPointDamage(Vec3 point, float radius, float impulse)
members.doc:
Server → every ghost: "this prop took a hit here". The point, radius
and impulse are enough because the pieces and their connectivity come
from the same bake on every peer.

members.name: MulticastBreak
members.signature: void MulticastBreak(uint32_t chunkSetId, uint32_t breakSeed, Vec3 impulse)
members.doc:
Server → every ghost: "this prop broke". Only the event is carried —
never the shards — so the wire cost is three words however many pieces
the bake holds. The system consumes the pending flag on its next tick,
because the RPC lands mid-frame and a break destroys the entity.

types.name: FDestructionBreakEvent
types.doc:
What the server sends once per break and what every peer replays.
`chunkSetId` names the bake the shards come from (0 = live carve from
the collider); `seed` only drives the per-piece launch jitter, because
the carve itself is fixed by the bake (or by the component's authored
seed) and must not vary between peers.

members.name: SetSceneHooks
members.doc:
Scene injects these so runtime-spawned pieces are registered with the
Scene's entity metadata (name, layers, render filter). Without hooks
the system falls back to raw World entities (headless tests).

members.name: ApplyDamageField
members.signature: void ApplyDamageField(const Vec3& center, float radius, float impulse)
members.doc:
Field-based damage: every Destructible whose position lies
within `radius` of `center` breaks, and its debris inherits an extra
velocity pointing away from the center, scaled by `impulse` and a
linear distance falloff — the explosion primitive (grenades, barrels,
spells). Enabled/broken state and cascades behave as in impact breaks.

members.name: BreakWithEvent
members.signature: bool BreakWithEvent(EntityID entity, const FDestructionBreakEvent& event)
members.doc:
Breaks `entity` from an explicit event — the client replay path, and
the way a test pins that two peers land the same shards.

members.name: ApplyPointDamage
members.signature: uint32_t ApplyPointDamage(EntityID entity, const Vec3& point, float radius, float impulse, bool fromNetwork = false)
members.doc:
Partial damage at a world point. `entity` is a Destructible with
Partial Damage on, or a remnant piece of one already hit. The pieces
within `radius` of the point are released as debris (pushed away from
the point by `impulse`), then everything left that cannot reach an
anchored piece through shared faces is released too. Returns the
number of pieces released; 0 when nothing was in range or the entity
is not damageable this way. The whole-prop break is what a
Destructible without Partial Damage does instead.

members.name: IsRemnantPiece
members.doc:
Remnant bookkeeping, for tests and tools: how many pieces of the
prop that `entity` belonged to are still standing, and whether an
entity is a standing remnant piece at all.

members.name: MakeBreakEvent
members.signature: FDestructionBreakEvent MakeBreakEvent(EntityID entity, const DestructibleComponent& dc)
members.doc: The event the host would send for a break of `entity` now.

members.name: PieceLaunchVelocity
members.signature: static Vec3 PieceLaunchVelocity(const FFracturePiece& piece, uint32_t pieceIndex, const Vec3& inheritedVelocity, float scatter, uint32_t seed)
members.doc:
Pure over its inputs: the same event lands the same shard the same
way on every peer, and a different seed lands it differently.

members.name: ResolveBake
members.doc:
Cached per path; a miss stays cached as null so a broken reference is
reported once rather than re-read on every break.

members.doc:
Seeds the cache directly — a headless test has no VFS to load from,
and a game that ships bakes inside its own archive can hand them over.

types.name: FFractureBakeData
types.doc:
An offline fracture: the Voronoi carve of one collider, stored so the
runtime never runs the clipper on the game thread and so every peer
breaks the prop into the SAME shards. `chunkSetId` is a content hash of
the piece payload — a break event names it, and a client whose bake
differs (stale cook, edited asset) knows to fall back rather than
spawn shards the server never had.

members.name: kSchemaVersion
members.doc:
v2 records the fracture method and its parameters; a v1 bake was a
uniform Voronoi carve and reads back as one.

members.name: method
members.doc:
The method the next bake carves with and its parameters; its piece
count and seed are `pieceCount` and `seed` above.

members.name: FracturePiecesForCollider
members.signature: static std::vector<FFracturePiece> FracturePiecesForCollider(const ColliderComponent* collider, uint32_t pieceCount, uint32_t seed, std::string* outSourceShape = nullptr, Vec3* outHalfExtents = nullptr)
members.doc:
The one carve the live path and the bake share: hull/mesh colliders
fracture their point cloud, spheres a fibonacci shell, everything else
(and any degenerate input) the box. Kept in one place so a baked prop
and an unbaked one shatter identically for the same seed.

types.name: EDestructionAnchor
types.doc:
Which pieces of a fracture hold the rest up. A piece is anchored when it
touches the named side of the fractured volume's bounds (within
`anchorMargin`); everything that cannot reach an anchored piece through
shared faces is unsupported and falls.

types.name: FFractureConnectivity
types.doc:
The connectivity of a fracture, computed from the pieces' geometry so a
bake and a live carve answer alike on every peer: two pieces are
neighbours when they share a face (coplanar, facing each other, and one
face's centre lies inside the other's polygon).

members.name: BuildAdjacency
members.signature: static std::vector<std::vector<uint32_t>> BuildAdjacency(const std::vector<FFracturePiece>& pieces, float epsilon = 1e-3f)
members.doc: adjacency[i] lists the neighbours of piece i.

members.name: FindAnchored
members.signature: static std::vector<bool> FindAnchored(const std::vector<FFracturePiece>& pieces, EDestructionAnchor anchor, float anchorMargin)
members.doc:
anchored[i] is true when piece i touches the anchor side of the
pieces' shared bounds. None anchors nothing, so any damage releases
the whole set.

members.name: FindSupported
members.signature: static std::vector<bool> FindSupported(const std::vector<std::vector<uint32_t>>& adjacency, const std::vector<bool>& anchored, const std::vector<bool>& alive)
members.doc:
supported[i] is true for every alive piece that reaches an alive
anchored piece through alive neighbours. Dead pieces are never
supported.

types.name: EFractureMethod
types.doc:
The fracture methods of UE's Fracture Mode the Destruction module carves.
Every one cuts a convex volume with planes, so every piece stays a convex
polyhedron the runtime can hull and the bake can store verbatim, and the
pieces always partition the volume.

types.name: EFractureBrickBond
types.doc: How a brick wall's courses are laid (the bonds UE's Brick fracture offers).

members.name: PieceCount
members.doc:
Uniform / Clustered / Radial / Planar: how many cells (Clustered: in
all clusters together) or cutting planes; Seed drives every jitter.

members.name: ClusterCount
members.doc:
Clustered: cells gather around this many centres, each spread over a
sphere of ClusterRadius × the volume's diagonal.

members.name: RadialCenter
members.doc:
Radial: rings of cells around a centre offset from the volume's middle,
in the plane normal to Y; Variability jitters angle and radius (0..1).

members.name: SlicesX
members.doc:
Planar: PieceCount random planes through the volume, each cutting every
piece it crosses.
Slice: evenly spaced cuts along each axis, tilted up to SliceAngle deg.

members.name: Bond
members.doc:
Brick: courses along Y of BrickHeight, bricks along X of BrickLength
(a header shows its BrickDepth end), wythes along Z of BrickDepth.

members.name: kMaxPieces
members.doc: The most pieces a bake may hold (the piece payload's decode cap).

members.name: BondFromName
members.signature: static bool BondFromName(const std::string& name, EFractureBrickBond& out)

members.name: FractureBox
members.signature: static std::vector<FFracturePiece> FractureBox(const Vec3& halfExtents, const FFractureMethodSettings& settings)
members.doc:
Carves the box of `halfExtents` (centred on the origin) by the method.
Uniform carves exactly what FVoronoiFracture::FractureBox does for the
same count and seed. Empty when the settings would exceed kMaxPieces.

members.name: FractureVolume
members.signature: static std::vector<FFracturePiece> FractureVolume(const std::vector<std::vector<Vec3>>& faces, const FFractureMethodSettings& settings)
members.doc: The same over any convex volume given as outward-wound face polygons.

members.name: EstimatePieces
members.signature: static uint32_t EstimatePieces(const Vec3& halfExtents, const FFractureMethodSettings& settings)
members.doc:
How many pieces the settings carve from that box, before carving: exact
for Slice and Brick (the cells the pattern lays over the box), the
requested count for Uniform and Clustered, an upper bound for Radial
(a ring outside the volume carves nothing) and Planar (the most cells
n planes can make).

members.name: FractureMeshPoints
members.signature: static std::vector<FFracturePiece> FractureMeshPoints(const std::vector<Vec3>& points, uint32_t pieceCount, uint32_t seed)
members.doc:
Fracture an arbitrary point cloud (mesh vertices, hull
collider points): the convex hull of the points becomes the fractured
volume, Voronoi seeds are rejection-sampled inside it, and the same
bisector clipping carves the cells. Non-convex meshes fracture as their
convex hull (the industry-standard debris approximation). Needs >= 4
non-coplanar points; returns empty on degenerate input.

types.name: VoxelDestructibleComponent
types.doc:
Voxel destruction: at play the entity's collider shape (box, sphere or
mesh) becomes a grid of voxels. Damage carves spheres out of it; the carved
voxels fly off as rubble chunks, and whatever no longer connects to the
floor (or to the largest piece) breaks away as one physics body per piece.

members.name: anchorFloor
members.doc:
Pieces stay up while they touch the bottom layer; off, the largest
piece stays and the rest fall.

members.name: rubbleChunk
members.doc: Carved voxels leave as chunks this many voxels across; 0 drops them.
